A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EPSVec and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Added analyses and relocated tables can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original synthetic-text generation experiments, downstream classification results, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional IMDb vector-extraction ablations in Appendix D.4–D.5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same vector extraction, privatization, fixed-shot selection, and steering procedures. Mean pooling remains the default; the added extraction variants are experimental ablations rather than revisions to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate IMDb, Yelp, BioRxiv, and OpenReview with the same tasks and populations. The new extraction ablations use existing IMDb coverage.

E2.justification: New Tables 6–7 introduce two ablation comparators: EPSVec++ with two real shots during extraction and EPSVec++ using final-token representations. The main comparison set, including AUG-PE, InvisibleInk, PP, PP++, and nonprivate controls, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4–D.5 adds controlled IMDb evaluations varying extraction-shot count and token aggregation at ε = 3 and 5 with pretrained models. Existing benchmark protocols, generation targets, metrics, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Two targeted ablations now test whether additional real extraction shots help and whether final-token extraction can replace mean pooling. Existing component, temperature, layer, privacy-budget, and rejection-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds for Table 2 and use the same plus/minus reporting style. The new ablation rows report ±0.0 without specifying their run counts; no changed uncertainty-estimation procedure or additional statistical test is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 add extraction-variant results. At ε = 5, two-real-shot extraction reports MAUVE/BERT scores of 64.6/82.0 and final-token extraction reports 66.5/87.6, against the retained default's 72.3/84.3. Additional results appear at ε = 3. Existing benchmark, figure, and rejection-sampling results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, equations, Theorems 4.1–4.2, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The added layer-count discussion explains the existing composition guarantee without introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reusable private dataset vectors, fixed-shot prompting, fidelity, and efficiency. Appendix F clarifies prior-work credit without changing these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 adds rationale connecting layer count to steering stability and privacy cost. D.4–D.5 interpret additional real shots as a mixed tradeoff and favor mean pooling for fidelity. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies that the existing two-shot baseline randomly selects private examples at every step. Conversely, v2 removes EPSVec's title-page code link. Other implementation details and prompts are retained; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual repository availability.

R1.justification: Appendix F explicitly credits prior private-generation work for using pretrained models and distinguishes EPSVec's reusable DP fixed-shots from direct real-data prompting. Bibliographic changes otherwise update retained works, including the Qwen3 reference, rather than expand literature coverage.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanatory additions, a revised final-discussion paragraph, baseline clarification, small language corrections, and bibliographic metadata edits. Two appendix subsections are inserted, while the overall narrative and section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: Two ablation tables are added. The extended-results table moves from Table 6 to Table 9, and the rejection-sampling table moves from Table 7 to Table 8 and nearer its discussion. Existing figure content is retained, with limited resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The new extraction ablations provide useful evidence for existing design choices, and the expanded discussion clarifies their tradeoffs and relationship to prior work. These modest gains outweigh the loss of the code pointer, although unspecified run counts behind the new ±0.0 entries limit the strength of the added evidence. Main results and proofs remain unchanged.
